_comment: TweakDB character records for everyone who has a body in a scene.
The shape is the one both reference mods ship: inherit a vanilla Character
record with $base and override only what differs. Hot Fuzz's entire NPC is two
lines (Character.judy_max: $base Character.Judy + entityTemplatePath), which is
the whole of the mechanism.
Every 'base' and 'appearance' below is VERIFIED against Appearance Menu Mod's
db.sqlite3 - its 'entities' table stores entity_path as a literal TweakDB record
name and joins to an 'appearances' table of valid appearance CNames. Nothing here
is invented; a record or appearance that AMM cannot spawn does not go in this file.
'marker' is a NodeRef to a worldStaticMarkerNode declared in source/world.json. It
becomes spawnDespawnParams.spawnMarkerNodeRef verbatim, which is how the engine
knows where to put her. It carries the leading '#' because throughout this project
a marker DEFINITION (world.json) is bare and a marker REFERENCE carries '#' - and
because validate.py finds every reference by scanning source/*.json for '#ac_*',
so writing it bare here would hide it from the typo and dead-weight checks.
The short '#name' form is deliberate and is what Hot Fuzz ships on this field
('#nq_judy_spawner'). The LONG '$/03_night_city/...' path is used only by a quest
node's sceneLocation. Same marker, two forms, two different fields.
'displayName' is a symbolic id in source/strings.json; tools/gen_tweak.py resolves
it through source/lockeys.json to the LocKey#N form TweakXL wants (rule 6).

_casting: Vanilla 'Female Suspicious Traveler' - a background traveller in Phantom
Liberty's q306 airport. Chosen for three reasons: her appearances are the only
ones in the game literally named 'fia_undercover', which is precisely what Mara
has been for nine years; she is a non-combat scene NPC, so nothing in her record
wants to shoot V; and no player will recognise her as somebody else, which using
a named NPC like Judy or Songbird would guarantee.

_alternatives._comment: Swapping 'base' + 'appearance' to any of these is a one-edit change. Each one changes how the player reads Mara BEFORE she speaks, which is the real decision.

dogtown_civilian.reads_as: nobody at all - fits 'spent nine years hoping nobody'd dig it back out'; 10 appearances to pick from

still_dangerous.reads_as: a threat in tactical kit - makes the opening line land as an ambush rather than a warning

characters._comment: Whoever tips V off. Deliberately never identified - the premise gives the hook to 'an unknown number' and Mr. Blue Eyes his own contact, so the question of who made this call is a hole the quest never fills. displayName reuses str.sms_unknown_title, the same string the phone contact is named with, so the nameplate on the subtitle and the name on the phone cannot drift apart into two different kinds of anonymous.

The two seconds of recording the caller plays down the line: V's own voice saying words V never said. It is a separate actor from V because V is in the scene, on the phone - a line hung on the player actor would be V speaking, not V being played back. The subtitle says RECORDING rather than a name because the phone has no idea who it is either; that ambiguity is the beat.

_comment: D130. Mr. Blue Eyes, for the one scene in this quest where he is a man
standing on a pavement rather than a number with no caller id.
Character.q203_mr_x is HIS OWN vanilla record, not a lookalike. Its
entityTemplatePath is the raRef hash 2012867658149774415, which is FNV1a64 of
base\quest\main_quests\epilogue\q203\characters\q203_mr_x.ent - and Appearance
Menu Mod's db lists that same record under the name 'Mr. Blue Eyes (G-Man)'
with exactly one appearance, the one named here. The record's own
appearanceName flat is empty, so naming it here is not an override of a
choice, it is supplying the one gen_scene.py needs.
corporat_ma__q003_gman is also the only place the game says out loud what he
is. The model was cut for q003 - the heist - and reused for the man who turns
up when everything is over.
displayName reuses sms_blueeyes_title - NO CALLER ID - exactly as the unknown
caller reuses sms_unknown_title (D126): the nameplate over his head and the
name on the phone are the same handle, because V never gets another one. It
is also how he is named in eighteen locales without inventing a translation
for a character the player has never heard V address by name.
No keepAlive, unlike Mara (D105): he is despawned the frame the scene ends.
That is the right picture for this man, and it also keeps a shootable
Character record off a Dogtown pavement - D127 is what that costs.

_voices: D126. 'voice': true marks a speaker with no body at all. They are cast only in
holocall scenes, where gen_scene.py builds them with voice_actor_def() -
acquisitionPlan findInContext, contextualName 'Voice' - so there is no entity to
place and nothing to stand anywhere.
Three tools read the flag. validate.py stops demanding a 'marker', because there
is no spawn for a missing marker to send to the world origin; gen_tweak.py stops
writing uiNameplate, because a nameplate is drawn over a head and these have
none; and validate.py refuses to let a voice be cast in a scene that is NOT a
holocall - the one way this flag could go wrong quietly, since actor_def() would
then want the marker that is no longer required.
Both inherit Character.q005_penthouse_siri, which is not a stand-in: it is the
record behind the penthouse AI in q005_07_vip_apartment - the one vanilla actor
on this machine that speaks without a body, and the same scene voice_actor_def()
was built field-for-field from. A bodiless speaker inheriting the bodiless
speaker is the honest $base; any walking NPC's record would have been a claim
about an appearance nobody can ever see.
_enemies: The Act 5 cleanup crew. Every vanilla FIA record (q305_fia_agent, q305_nusa_agent,
q307_fia_av_agent, q306_fia_agent_corpo_scene_*) is friendly or neutral and carries
no weapon, so none of them can fight. These inherit the NetWatch field agents of
mws_se5_06 - suits, a rifle and a handgun loadout, full archetypeData - and override
one flat: baseAttitudeGroup 'hostile' (Attitudes.Group_Hostile: Hostile to Group_Player,
Friendly to itself and to everyone else, so they do not start a war with Barghest).
168 vanilla Character records ship baseAttitudeGroup hostile. No appearance override:
the base's own appearance list is used, so there is nothing to verify against AMM.
No nameplate either - an enemy gets the game's default combat nameplate.

player._record: Not ours and not overridden - this is the vanilla player puppet, read off the Undermine template's scnPlayerActorDef. V is acquired with findInContext, never spawned.
